$comment: tools/cpu-sweep.ts reads this. `machines` scales each CPU model to the AMD EPYC 7763 (factor 1): a factor is the median, over routes confirmed in every run, of the route's raw median on the 7763 divided by its raw median on that model, from `runs` runs (2026-10-09). The 9V45's 1.484 came from 2 runs, and its runs read a median 5.8% under their reference routes where the 7763's read 0.5% under, so it was refit on 2026-11-20 from 22 runs against 33 EPYC 7763 runs of the CPU job, over `reference.routes`, since no route was re-sampled in every run: 1.586, with a bootstrap 5th to 95th percentile of 1.525 to 1.619. A model with no entry reads raw and --gate judges nothing on it; a model needs two runs before it gets a factor. No laptop is listed: a laptop's other work inflates every reading at once (an M3 Max read 1.7x higher on one run than the run before), so a local run reads raw and gets no verdict. `routes` lets a route stay up to its own ceilingMs, in EPYC 7763 ms, with the reason it costs that much today: the highest of 14 scaled CI runs plus 20%, rounded up to the half millisecond, for every route whose highest reading plus 20% passed the 8 ms gate. --gate fails on an entry for a route the sweep doesn't know, and prints an entry whose route reads under 4 ms as stale, so the list only shrinks. A row re-fit since then carries `measured`: how many conclusive CI runs it was fit on, their p50, p99 and highest in EPYC 7763 ms, and the date. Its ceiling is that highest plus 20%, rounded up to the half millisecond, and contract-cpu-sweep-can-tell-slow-from-fast holds it there (gotcha 81). `reference.routes` is each heavy route's usual median in EPYC 7763 ms: every route whose median read 5 ms or more over 24 calibrated CI runs of the CPU job after #1771's fixes (2026-11-20). A run whose routes, scaled, read more than `reference.drift` off them, at the median of their ratios, is inconclusive (gotcha 57). With references fit the same way, 167 ordinary runs from 2026-11-13 to 11-20 read from 18% under to 10% over, and the 11 slow EPYC 9V74s read 25% to 37% over. If every run starts to drift the same way, the routes' own cost moved: refit `routes` from 20 or more calibrated CI runs.

/agent-ready.why: the sweep refuses outbound fetch, so this times the probe's error path, not a real check; not profiled yet

/photos/query.json?q=classic+chrome+brid.why: parses the four photo JSON files (metadata, alt text, thumb hashes, semantics), decodes the build-time ranking index (lib/photo-search.ts) and ranks from it, then serializes 100; the index took this route from 12.6 to 9.1 raw ms in a local A/B on 2026-11-03, and the ceiling waits on CI runs to refit

/photos/query.json?q=red+car.why: the same parse, index decode and ranking as the 100-result query, serializing 25

/ask?query=dictionary.why: the cold search prepare /search pays, then KV reads and Analytics Engine writes it makes in production too (#1266 measured them at about 2.2 raw ms)

/finger.why: renders the finger terminal frame per request (it's in config/per-request-pages.json); not profiled yet

/search?q=brotli.why: search.ts prepares every record of the site index on first use and caches it per isolate, so a cold request pays the whole prepare; not profiled since #1208

/search.json?q=what+does+he+think+about+.why: the same cold search prepare as /search

POST /mcp search_site.why: the same cold search prepare as /search, behind the MCP server's JSON-RPC handling

/photos/query.json.why: parses the four photo JSON files even with no query to score

/reading/list.html.why: an island fragment rendered per request; the sweep's empty KV times only the no-links fallback, so this ceiling says nothing about the 120-link render production does, whose per-row date formatters came out on 2026-10-09 (9.8 to 6.0 ms cold under node with the real KV values)

/search.json?q=brotli.why: the same cold search prepare as /search

/this-page-does-not-exist.why: the not-found page, rendered per request; since #1386 a caller that names text/html, as the sweep does, gets a Luna window from lunaPage, which read 1.0 raw ms over the plain-text 404 in a local A/B (2026-10-17). Re-fit from the CI runs after it (gotcha 81); a 404 regression under about 5 ms passes this ceiling
